entries.name: GRNT
entries.description: Granite: igneous silicate rock, density 2700 kg/m3, k=2.8 W/mK, begins melting ~1215-1260C. Acid-resistant except HF.
entries.use: Generic hard structural stone / statuary that resists most acids and abrasion.

entries.name: BSLT
entries.description: Basalt: fine-grained volcanic rock, density 3000 kg/m3, k=1.9 W/mK, melts ~1200C back into lava.
entries.use: Dense aggregate / basalt-fiber precursor for heavy foundations and armor fill.

entries.name: LMST
entries.description: Limestone (CaCO3): density 2600 kg/m3, k=1.3 W/mK, calcines above ~825-900C releasing CO2 gas, leaving lime.
entries.use: Classic acid-vulnerable masonry stone; calcines to CO2 gas when fired, exactly like a real lime kiln.

entries.name: MRBL
entries.description: Marble (metamorphosed CaCO3): density 2700 kg/m3, k=2.7 W/mK, calcines ~900C releasing CO2. Dissolves in weak acid (acid rain damage).
entries.use: Decorative facade/sculpture stone; famously eaten by acid rain, so it deliberately has very low acid resistance.

entries.name: SDST
entries.description: Sandstone: quartz-cemented sedimentary rock, density 2300 kg/m3, k=2.0 W/mK, silica component melts ~1650C.
entries.use: Porous, quartz-rich building stone, good acid resistance, poor insulator.

entries.name: FBRK
entries.description: Fired clay brick: density 1900 kg/m3, k=0.8 W/mK, vitrifies/melts ~1150C. Classic load-bearing masonry unit.
entries.use: Standard fired masonry unit for walls and kilns; decent insulator, decent acid resistance.

entries.name: RCNC
entries.description: Reinforced concrete (steel rebar mesh in 2400 kg/m3 concrete, k=1.7 W/mK). Rebar corrodes; spalls ~300C under fire load.
entries.use: Structural slab/column material that actually conducts via its rebar mesh, unlike plain shielding concrete (CNCR).

entries.name: ASPH
entries.description: Asphalt (bitumen concrete): density 2300 kg/m3, k=0.75 W/mK, softens ~50-60C, decomposes to tar fumes ~300C.
entries.use: Road/roofing surface material; soft, low acid resistance to solvents, decomposes into smoke when overheated.

entries.name: GYPS
entries.description: Gypsum board (CaSO4*2H2O): density 800 kg/m3, k=0.17 W/mK, dehydrates/calcines ~150C releasing bound water.
entries.use: Passive fire-rated partition wall; vents steam and calcines instead of burning, exactly like real drywall.

entries.name: OAK
entries.description: Oak timber: density 750 kg/m3, k=0.17 W/mK, autoignites ~300C. Tannin-rich, historically used for acid-resistant barrels.
entries.use: Dense structural hardwood; unusually acid/rot resistant for a timber, used for framing and casks.

entries.name: PINE
entries.description: Pine timber (softwood): density 500 kg/m3, k=0.12 W/mK, resinous, autoignites ~250C.
entries.use: Cheap, light softwood framing lumber; ignites more readily than oak.

entries.name: BAMB
entries.description: Bamboo culm: density 700 kg/m3, k=0.17 W/mK, autoignites ~300C. High tensile strength for its weight.
entries.use: Fast-growing eco-friendly scaffolding/framing material with steel-comparable tensile strength per weight.

entries.name: RBAR
entries.description: Mild-steel rebar: density 7850 kg/m3, k=50 W/mK, melts ~1500C. Conducts; rusts easily (low corrosion resistance).
entries.use: Tension reinforcement embedded in concrete; a plain conductive structural steel distinct from reactor-grade STEL.

entries.name: S316
entries.description: 316 stainless steel: density 8000 kg/m3, k=16 W/mK, melts ~1400C. Mo-alloyed, excellent chloride/acid resistance.
entries.use: Marine and chemical-process grade stainless; the corrosion-proof alternative to plain RBAR/STEL.

entries.name: AL61
entries.description: Aluminium 6061-T6: density 2700 kg/m3, k=167 W/mK, melts 582-652C. Self-passivating oxide layer. 2026-08-26 two-stage thermite: FIRE preheats without consuming AL61; at 480K it converts BRMT to IRON and itself to low-conductivity FSLG slag.
entries.use: Lightweight structural/aerospace alloy for frames and heat sinks; excellent conductor, moderate corrosion resistance.

entries.name: TI64
entries.description: Ti-6Al-4V titanium alloy: density 4430 kg/m3, k=6.7 W/mK, melts ~1650C. Exceptional strength-to-weight and corrosion resistance.
entries.use: Aerospace/medical-implant grade titanium alloy; among the best corrosion resistance of any structural metal.

entries.name: WC
entries.description: Tungsten carbide: density 15600 kg/m3, k=100 W/mK, decomposes/melts ~2870C. Near-diamond wear resistance for cutting tools.
entries.use: Extreme wear-resistant tooling/drill-bit material; second only to diamond for erosion resistance in this catalog.

entries.name: INC7
entries.description: Inconel 718 nickel superalloy: density 8190 kg/m3, k=11.4 W/mK, melts ~1300C. Retains strength & corrosion resistance red-hot.
entries.use: Turbine-blade/high-temperature aerospace alloy that stays strong and corrosion-resistant well past where steel fails.

entries.name: CIRN
entries.description: Grey cast iron: density 7200 kg/m3, k=55 W/mK, melts ~1200C (lower than steel due to carbon content). Brittle, rusts.
entries.use: Classic heavy machinery/engine-block/cookware alloy; cheap, castable, but corrodes and cracks rather than bends.

entries.name: MWOL
entries.description: Mineral (rock) wool batt: k=0.04 W/mK, non-combustible, fibers melt/slag ~1100C.
entries.use: Non-combustible thermal/acoustic insulation batt for walls and ducts.

entries.name: PUFM
entries.description: Closed-cell polyurethane foam: k=0.024 W/mK (near-aerogel), decomposes ~250C releasing toxic fumes. Burns readily.
entries.use: Spray-foam wall/roof insulation with best-in-class k-value, but a serious fire/toxic-smoke hazard.

entries.name: CFIB
entries.description: Carbon-fibre composite (CFRP): density 1600 kg/m3, k~5 W/mK along fibre, resin chars ~380C. Mildly conductive.
entries.use: Ultra-light, very stiff structural composite for aerospace/racing panels.

entries.name: GFIB
entries.description: Glass-fibre (fiberglass) batt: k=0.038 W/mK, softens/melts ~850C. Non-combustible.
entries.use: Cheap non-combustible thermal insulation batt, softer variant of mineral wool.

entries.name: KEVL
entries.description: Kevlar (para-aramid): density 1440 kg/m3, k=0.04 W/mK, chars/decomposes ~450C rather than melting.
entries.use: Ballistic-rated fabric/composite for armor and cut-resistant rope, self-extinguishing.

entries.name: PTFE
entries.description: PTFE (Teflon): density 2200 kg/m3, k=0.25 W/mK, melts 327C, decomposes to toxic fumes above melt. Nearly chemically inert.
entries.use: Near-universal chemical resistance liner/seal/low-friction coating; one of the least reactive plastics known.

entries.name: PVC
entries.description: PVC (rigid): density 1400 kg/m3, k=0.19 W/mK, softens ~80C, decomposes ~140-200C releasing HCl fumes.
entries.use: Cheap rigid plastic pipe/conduit/siding with good acid resistance but toxic combustion products.

entries.name: HDPE
entries.description: HDPE: density 950 kg/m3, k=0.45-0.5 W/mK, melts ~130C. Outstanding chemical resistance, flammable when molten.
entries.use: Chemical-tank/pipe plastic prized for near-universal solvent and acid resistance.

entries.name: NYLN
entries.description: Nylon 6,6: density 1140 kg/m3, k=0.25 W/mK, melts ~265C. Moderate acid resistance, degrades in strong acids.
entries.use: Tough engineering plastic for gears, rope, and fasteners.

entries.name: SILR
entries.description: Silicone rubber: density 1200 kg/m3, k=0.2 W/mK, stable to ~300C then decomposes. Good chemical/UV resistance.
entries.use: High-temperature gaskets and seals that outlast ordinary rubber in heat and sun.

entries.name: RUBR
entries.description: Natural (latex) rubber: density 920 kg/m3, k=0.13 W/mK, decomposes/vulcanizate chars ~200C. Degrades with ozone/oils.
entries.use: Vibration-damping/gasket rubber; cheap but ages and degrades faster than synthetic rubbers.

entries.name: ALUM
entries.description: Alumina (Al2O3) ceramic: density 3950 kg/m3, k=30 W/mK, melts 2072C. Chemically near-inert, used for acid-resistant linings.
entries.use: Hard, chemically inert technical ceramic for insulators, seals, and acid-tank linings.

entries.name: ZRCA
entries.description: Zirconia (ZrO2): density 5680 kg/m3, k=2 W/mK, melts 2715C. Extremely inert, used in dental/chemical apparatus.
entries.use: Ultra-refractory, chemically bulletproof ceramic for crucibles, valves, and dental parts.

entries.name: SIC
entries.description: Silicon carbide: density 3210 kg/m3, k=120 W/mK, decomposes/sublimes ~2700C. Semiconductor; used in power electronics.
entries.use: Extremely hard, high-thermal-conductivity abrasive/refractory that also works as a wide-bandgap semiconductor.

entries.name: BORO
entries.description: Borosilicate glass: density 2230 kg/m3, k=1.2 W/mK, softens ~820C. Low thermal expansion, resists most acids (attacked by HF).
entries.use: Lab glassware / oven-safe cookware glass valued for thermal shock and chemical resistance.

entries.name: FSIL
entries.description: Fused silica (SiO2 glass): density 2200 kg/m3, k=1.4 W/mK, softens ~1650C. Exceptional chemical/thermal resistance, used in optics.
entries.use: Premium optical/semiconductor-furnace glass; best chemical and thermal-shock resistance of common glasses.

entries.name: CTIL
entries.description: Glazed ceramic tile: density 2300 kg/m3, k=1.0 W/mK, melts/vitrifies further ~1200C. Resists most household acids.
entries.use: Acid- and moisture-resistant flooring/wall cladding for labs, kitchens, bathrooms.

entries.name: SIPV
entries.description: Monocrystalline silicon PV cell: ~22% sunlight-to-electricity efficiency, melts 1414C, k=150 W/mK. Attacked only by HF.
entries.use: PHOT-driven solar cell: converts incoming light into SPRK at realistic ~22% efficiency.

entries.name: GERM
entries.description: Germanium: density 5323 kg/m3, k=60 W/mK, melts 938C. Semiconductor, moderate acid resistance (attacked by oxidizers).
entries.use: Early transistor/infrared-optics semiconductor material, distinct from silicon's band gap and IR transparency.

entries.name: GAAS
entries.description: Gallium arsenide: density 5320 kg/m3, k=55 W/mK, melts 1238C. High-efficiency (~28%) space-grade PV / RF semiconductor.
entries.use: High-efficiency, radiation-tolerant photovoltaic used on satellites; outperforms silicon PV per area.

entries.name: PZT
entries.description: Lead zirconate titanate ceramic: Curie point ~360C, density 8060 kg/m3, k~1.5 W/mK. Generates charge under mechanical stress.
entries.use: Pressure-to-SPRK piezoelectric transducer for sensors, igniters, and sonar drivers.

entries.name: NBTI
entries.description: Niobium-titanium alloy: superconducts below Tc=9.3K, density 6000 kg/m3, k~9 W/mK at room temp, melts ~1950C.
entries.use: Superconducting-magnet wire (MRI, particle-accelerator coils); modeled as an excellent normal-state conductor.

entries.name: GRPN
entries.description: Graphene monolayer: in-plane k up to ~5000 W/mK (highest known), essentially chemically inert carbon sheet, best known electrical conductor.
entries.use: Best-in-class heat spreader / conductor for high-density electronics stacks.

entries.name: FLBE
entries.description: FLiBe (2LiF-BeF2) molten salt: melts 459C, boils ~1400C, k=1.1 W/mK. Molten-salt reactor coolant/fuel carrier.
entries.use: Molten-salt reactor primary coolant; low vapor pressure, freezes solid (SALT) if it cools below melting.

entries.name: LHE
entries.description: Liquid helium-4: boils at 4.2K, density 125 kg/m3, k=0.02 W/mK. No native freezing point at 1 atm.
entries.use: Cryogen for cooling superconducting magnets (e.g. NBTI) below their critical temperature.

entries.name: LH2
entries.description: Liquid hydrogen: boils at 20.3K, density 71 kg/m3, k=0.1 W/mK. Rocket fuel, boils into HYGN gas.
entries.use: Cryogenic rocket-fuel liquid; boils into flammable HYGN gas just above 20K.

entries.name: ARGN
entries.description: Argon gas: inert, boils/condenses at 87.3K, density 1.78 kg/m3 (STP), k(gas)=0.0177 W/mK.
entries.use: Inert shielding gas for welding and an inert purge/backfill gas for reactive-metal work.

entries.name: H2O2
entries.description: Hydrogen peroxide (concentrated): density 1450 kg/m3, decomposes exothermically ~150C into water+oxygen, corrosive/oxidizing. 2026-08-26: MG-catalyzed decay uses conc=20 (~5 hits to fully convert); explosive flag fixed 15->0.
entries.use: High-test peroxide oxidizer/monopropellant and industrial bleach/disinfectant; corrosive on contact.

entries.name: KERO
entries.description: Kerosene/Jet-A: density 810 kg/m3, flash point ~50C, distills/burns ~150-300C, k=0.14 W/mK.
entries.use: Jet-fuel-grade liquid hydrocarbon for combustion/rocket-propellant builds, safer to store than gasoline.

entries.name: BDSL
entries.description: Biodiesel (FAME): density 880 kg/m3, flash point ~130-170C (high, safer than diesel), boils/decomposes ~300C, k=0.17 W/mK.
entries.use: Renewable diesel substitute; harder to ignite than petrodiesel, biodegradable.

entries.name: ETOH
entries.description: Ethanol: density 789 kg/m3, boils 78.4C, flash point 13C (very flammable), k=0.17 W/mK.
entries.use: Common flammable-fuel/solvent liquid (E85, biofuel, disinfectant base) that flash-boils into flammable vapor.

entries.name: GLYC
entries.description: Glycerol: density 1261 kg/m3, boils/decomposes ~290C (releases acrolein fumes), k=0.29 W/mK. Low flammability, viscous.
entries.use: Viscous, low-flammability liquid for hydraulic/heat-transfer or antifreeze mixes.

entries.name: LBE
entries.description: Lead-bismuth eutectic (44.5Pb-55.5Bi): melts 123.5C, boils 1670C, high thermal conductivity liquid metal.
entries.use: Fast-reactor liquid-metal coolant that stays liquid far below lead's own melting point; freezes into LEAD (power-elements set) when cold.

entries.name: PCMP
entries.description: Paraffin-wax PCM (RT58-type): melts 58C, latent heat ~200 kJ/kg. Absorbs/releases heat at constant temperature.
entries.use: Passive thermal-buffer wax: soaks up excess heat at 58C and releases it back later instead of just heating up.

entries.name: PCMS
entries.description: Sodium sulfate decahydrate (Glauber's salt) PCM: melts 32C, latent heat ~251 kJ/kg. Cheap high-density heat buffer.
entries.use: Low-temperature (near room-temp) latent heat store for solar-thermal or off-peak heat buffering.

entries.name: NAS
entries.description: Molten sodium-sulfur (NaS) battery couple: operates 300-350C, freezes solid below ~300C, sodium boils 883C.
entries.use: Grid-scale molten-salt battery electrolyte; must stay hot (300C+) to function, freezes solid (SALT) if it cools.

entries.name: DU
entries.description: Depleted uranium: density 19100 kg/m3 (same as natural U), melts 1132C, k=27 W/mK. Much less radioactive than URAN; valued for density.
entries.use: Ultra-dense armor/penetrator/counterweight metal; deliberately far less radioactive than native URAN.

entries.name: THOR
entries.description: Thorium metal: density 11700 kg/m3, melts 1750C, k=54 W/mK. Weakly radioactive (Th-232, half-life 14 billion years); breeder fuel.
entries.use: Fertile breeder-reactor fuel material (Th-232 to U-233), weakly radioactive.

entries.name: BE
entries.description: Beryllium metal: density 1850 kg/m3, melts 1287C, k=200 W/mK. Neutron-transparent reflector; toxic dust hazard.
entries.use: Neutron reflector around a reactor core (like ZIRC/GRPH, lets neutrons pass to bounce them back in).

entries.name: HF
entries.description: Hafnium metal: density 13300 kg/m3, melts 2233C, k=23 W/mK. Very high thermal-neutron capture cross-section, excellent corrosion resistance.
entries.use: Premium long-life reactor control-rod material; absorbs neutrons and survives reactor coolant chemistry far longer than CD.

entries.name: CD
entries.description: Cadmium metal: density 8650 kg/m3, melts only 321C, k=97 W/mK. Very high neutron capture cross-section; used in the first Chicago Pile control rods.
entries.use: Historic, fast-acting neutron-poison control-rod material; melts far more easily than HF/B4C so use it away from hot fuel.

entries.name: BPE
entries.description: Borated polyethylene (20 wt% boron): density 1650 kg/m3, k=0.4 W/mK, melts ~130C. Cheap hydrogen-rich neutron shield.
entries.use: Low-cost neutron-shielding wall for moderating and absorbing stray NEUT around a reactor room.

entries.name: PCAR
entries.description: Polycarbonate: density 1200 kg/m3, k=0.2 W/mK, softens ~150C, decomposes ~300C. Impact-resistant glazing.
entries.use: Bullet/impact-resistant transparent glazing panel, tougher than acrylic or glass.

entries.name: CORK
entries.description: Cork (natural bark): density 200 kg/m3, k=0.04 W/mK, chars ~350-400C. Rot- and moisture-resistant natural insulator.
entries.use: Lightweight natural insulation/flooring material, renewable and rot-resistant.

entries.name: BRSS
entries.description: Brass (Cu-Zn alloy): density 8500 kg/m3, k=120 W/mK, melts ~930-940C. Good conductor, moderate corrosion resistance.
entries.use: Plumbing fittings, musical instruments, and low-friction fasteners/bearings.

entries.name: BRNZ
entries.description: Bronze (Cu-Sn alloy): density 8800 kg/m3, k=70 W/mK, melts ~950C. Harder and more corrosion-resistant than brass.
entries.use: Statuary/bearing/marine-hardware alloy prized for resisting seawater corrosion.

entries.name: EPDM
entries.description: EPDM rubber: density 1150 kg/m3, k=0.25 W/mK, decomposes ~250C. Outstanding weathering/ozone/chemical resistance.
entries.use: Roofing membrane and outdoor weatherseal rubber that resists UV, ozone, and most chemicals far better than natural rubber.

entries.name: NA
entries.description: Sodium metal: melts 98 C, boils 883 C; reacts violently with water -> H2 + NaOH(aq) + ~600 K, ignites the hydrogen.
entries.use: real alkali-metal/water chemistry demo; hazard source

entries.name: MG
entries.description: Magnesium metal: melts 650 C; once ignited (~630 C) burns at ~3100 C in air producing MgO ash (STNE) and intense white light. 2026-08-26: FIRE-branch now consumes a real O2 neighbour (needs=O2=NONE).
entries.use: flare/thermite igniter, needs oxygen

entries.name: CAO
entries.description: Quicklime CaO: reacts exothermically with water (slaking, +~300 K) to hydrated lime (clay-like solid); melts 2613 C.
entries.use: exothermic non-flammable heat source, mortar chemistry

entries.name: CAC2
entries.description: Calcium carbide CaC2: with water releases acetylene gas (flammable) + lime, mildly exothermic; melts 2160 C. 2026-08-26: reaction now also adds pgas=8 sim.pressure per event (carbide-gas-generator).
entries.use: carbide lamp / acetylene generator

entries.name: FSLG
entries.description: Thermite slag (solidified Al2O3/Fe-oxide mix): k~3 W/mK (low, real molten-oxide diffusivity), density ~4200 kg/m3 (rough estimate). Deliberately low HeatConduct so a reacted AL61/BRMT cell holds heat instead of flash-averaging away in one conduction frame.
entries.use: Thermite reaction product (AL61 two-stage rule); inert afterwards.
